name: adiabatic_saturation_wet_bulb
title: Adiabatic saturation and wet-bulb temperature of moist air
summary: Air at 25 degC dry bulb and 15 degC wet bulb at 1 atm: specific humidity, relative humidity and specific enthalpy of the moist air per kg of dry air, obtained with the adiabatic-saturation formula of the course (mass and energy balances of a wet-bulb thermometer, constant heat capacities) and cross-checked with the EES property functions HumRat, RelHum and enthalpy.

authors: TBD (ULiège course Thermodynamique appliquée, MECA0002 - see README 'Source and attribution')
origin.course: ULiège Thermodynamique appliquée (MECA0002), exercise session R9 (2022-2023), exercise 5

verification.reference: Solution stored in the original EES file R09_E05_2022.EES (EES 10.836); the three humid-air property calls were also recomputed with the CoolProp Python library (v8.0.0) and the humidity ratio compared with the ASHRAE wet-bulb relation
verification.notes: Hand-converted from kPa/kJ. compare_solution.py --ees-units: 26 common variables, 2 above rtol 1e-3, largest relative deviation 5.24e-03 (omega_db_bis, EES HumRat: CoolProp moist air carries the water-enhancement factor, 0.53 % above the course formula omega_db, itself within 1.12e-04 of EES; the same effect was measured at +0.42 % on CSL-0055) and 3.08e-03 (h_db_bis, absolute moist-air enthalpy: different reference state/formulation, the course definition h_db agreeing with both at 4.46e-05). Every other variable agrees at 8.47e-04 or better. Second check: HAPropsSI('W'/'H'/'R','T',298.15,'B',288.15,'P',101325) reproduces omega_db_bis, h_db_bis and RH_db_bis exactly. Third check: the ASHRAE wet-bulb relation gives 0.00652176 kg/kg against 0.00652554 of the model (5.8e-04). The 44 variables of the EES file that are not in the model are the stale leftovers of an earlier exercise of the same file (h[1..7], p[1..7], T[1..7], s[1..7], v[1..7], x[1], x[3..7], P, cp, h_g_wb_bis2).
